days.title: The first evening.
days.lede: Dinner and a little browsing in Bangkok.

stops.title: NH Bangkok Sukhumvit Boulevard
stops.short: An overnight base in Bangkok’s Nana district, just off Sukhumvit Road. NH Bangkok Sukhumvit Boulevard pairs contemporary rooms with a rooftop pool and nearby Skytrain access—a city-hotel beginning before the journey moves north.
paragraphs: NH Bangkok Sukhumvit Boulevard stands on Sukhumvit Soi 5, close to Nana BTS. Its location belongs to Bangkok's busy modern shopping and restaurant corridor, rather than the older riverside quarters.
The hotel combines contemporary interiors with an outdoor rooftop pool, a gym and Tropicana, its all-day restaurant. The Bangkok booking covers 25–26 October, before the Chiang Mai chapter.
stops.note: Confirmed booking dates. Booking dates are not exact check-in or check-out times.

sources.label: NH Bangkok Sukhumvit Boulevard · official overview

stops.title: Sukhumvit · dinner and city browsing
paragraphs: The first dinner photograph records a whole fish topped with vegetables and cashews, with rice alongside. Later, cork handbags and purses beneath a UNI CORK sign turn the camera toward materials and small useful objects—a thread that continues in Chiang Mai.

The hotel base is Nana, on Sukhumvit Soi 5. Asok is the nearby shopping-and-transit junction farther along Sukhumvit, where the elevated BTS and underground MRT meet beside Terminal 21. The layered cityscape—rail lines above traffic, shops and restaurants below—gives this first evening its wider Bangkok setting.

The Asok photograph is a credited 2019 neighbourhood reference, not a scene captured on the trip. The dinner restaurant remains unnamed: the meal image has no readable venue sign, and its coarse location record is not precise enough to identify a particular kitchen.
stops.note: Asok is neighbourhood context, not a reconstructed walking route or a claim of a Terminal 21 visit. Nearby recommendations have not been turned into a restaurant identification.
stops.short: Sukhumvit’s restaurant-lined lanes and elevated trains frame the Bangkok beginning. Nearby Asok is the junction where BTS meets MRT beside Terminal 21; the evening’s own photographs stay closer to the table and the shop displays.

days.title: Teak houses, then north.
days.lede: Jim Thompson in Bangkok, then BED Nimman in Chiang Mai.

stops.title: Jim Thompson House Museum
paragraphs: The afternoon follows red teak verandas, courtyard umbrellas, orchids and collected objects, ending with a wall of silk colours. The architectural drawing and Jim Thompson merchandise help connect these photographs to the house and its heritage quarter.

Jim Thompson assembled this home from six old teak houses, including buildings brought from the Ayutthaya area and a house from the Cham weaving community of Ban Krua. Carpenters from Ayutthaya reassembled the structures in 1958–59; their raised floors, timber frames and garden setting remain central to its character.

The canal links the house to the weavers who worked with Thompson. His home was also a setting for his Asian art and antiques, so the museum brings two interests together: the reuse of traditional architecture and the collecting of objects across cultures.
stops.note: The drawing and Jim Thompson label establish a high-confidence match to the museum complex; the venue is also named in your later request. The four photographs are dated 26 October, with no usable GPS.

sources.label: Jim Thompson House Museum · The Thai House
Jim Thompson Heritage Quarter · House Museum

stops.short: Six traditional teak houses became one remarkable Bangkok home. Reassembled in 1958–59 beside the Ban Krua weaving community, the compound joins Thai timber architecture, a tropical garden and Jim Thompson’s collection of Asian art.

stops.title: BED Nimman
stops.short: Opened in 2016, BED Nimman offers a pared-back base among the neighbourhood’s cafés and small shops. Modern rooms, a tree-shaded pool and the hotel’s BED Deli breakfast give it a simple, informal character.
paragraphs: BED Nimman opened in 2016 in Chiang Mai's Nimman Haemin district. Its straightforward modern design places the emphasis on shared hospitality and easy access to the surrounding cafés, restaurants and shops.
The property has a swimming pool shaded by trees and serves its BED Deli breakfast. It was the first Chiang Mai base from 26 October; later trip receipts also place the traveller here on the 28th.
stops.note: The located booking is for 26–27 October. Airport-transfer and later trip receipts establish BED as a base on 26 and 28 October; the exact extension and checkout date remain unverified.

BED Hotels · official site

days.title: Coffee, craft, and Kao Soy.
days.region: Chiang Mai · Nimman & the Old City
days.lede: Coffee, the waterfall’s edge, craft and a favourite bowl of noodles.

stops.title: ROAST8RY Flagship
paragraphs: The photographed sign identifies the Nimman flagship. No drink order is inferred.
ROAST8RY's flagship opened in 2022 on Nimman Soi 17. The brand's work extends beyond the café counter: it sources coffee internationally and roasts beans for its own drinks and retail coffee range.

Its founder, Arnon Thitiprasert, won the 2017 World Latte Art Championship in Budapest. That competition background helps explain the attention to milk texture and presentation that accompanies the shop's specialty-coffee focus.

sources.label: ROAST8RY · official story and coffee
Loveramics · 2017 World Latte Art Championships

stops.short: ROAST8RY’s Nimman flagship connects the coffee bar to a wider roasting practice. Opened in 2022, it brings carefully sourced beans, espresso technique and latte-art expertise into a spare, contemporary space on Soi 17.

stops.title: Huay Kaew Waterfall
stops.short: At the foot of Doi Suthep, Huay Kaew marks the shift from Chiang Mai’s streets to forest. The roughly ten-metre cascade, rocky pools and shaded surroundings make it a small natural retreat close to the city.
paragraphs: Your photographs remember the waterfall stop through its food stalls: preparation at a chopping block and a sleeping dog in the lane. The cascade view is a separately credited reference photograph.

Huay Kaew lies within Doi Suthep–Pui National Park, close to Chiang Mai Zoo and the start of the mountain road. The national tourism directory describes a waterfall about ten metres high, surrounded by shade and woodland.
Rather than a remote expedition, this is a city-edge landscape of flowing water, rocks and forest. Its scale is intimate: cascades lead into lower pools, with places to pause beside the stream.
stops.note: Location supplied by you; date and times come from the matching original album photos. No swim, specific walking route or view of the cascade is inferred.

stops.title: Villa Nard · a salad lunch
stops.short: Australian-style brunch meets a Korean-influenced café in Santitham: coffee, salads, pancakes and pasta downstairs, with Fimue’s vintage and secondhand finds upstairs. It brings the food and browsing threads of the trip into one stop.
paragraphs: Shrimp, noodles, avocado and greens are the lunch recorded here. Your memory of the attached thrift and antique shop, together with the original recommendation, identifies Villa Nard.

Villa Nard is a brunch café on Morakot Road in Santitham. Its menu spans salads, pancakes, pasta and homemade sandwiches, with coffee and other drinks. Large windows, pale surfaces and vintage furnishings give the interior a light, domestic scale.

The upstairs Fimue shop adds vintage, secondhand and small craft objects to the visit. That combination distinguishes Villa Nard from a straightforward lunch stop: a café below, with another room of objects to explore above.
stops.note: High-confidence identification from your attached-shop description, the original lunch recommendation, address and photographed timing. No exact dish name is inferred.

stops.title: Kalm Village / MOM
paragraphs: The visit moves from MOM’s signed entrance to timber screens, a loom, a tall sculpture beside the windows and suspended cords beneath the timber ceiling.

Kalm Village reinterprets the shared spaces of a traditional Thai home: separate buildings serve different purposes but meet around communal courtyards. Old teak houses supplied reclaimed timber for the complex, paired with dark grey brick and contemporary Asian design.

The Museum of Makers is part of Kalm, presenting traditional and contemporary makers across disciplines. Its textile archive sits alongside rotating exhibitions, while the wider village supports workshops, residencies, a library and places to eat and gather.

sources.label: Kalm Village · About
Museum of Makers · official Kalm page
Kalm Village · Visit
The Weight of the World · 2024 archive

stops.short: Nine buildings, two shared courtyards and a material palette of dark brick and reclaimed teak: Kalm makes architecture part of its craft programme. MOM, its Museum of Makers, houses textile collections and changing exhibitions.

stops.title: Kao Soy Nimman
paragraphs: The carved restaurant sign and illuminated courtyard record the evening stop. The next day you wrote, “I loved kao soy.” The shared album’s meal frame was already partly eaten, so the signed frontage leads this entry.

Kao Soy Nimman specialises in variations of khao soi on Nimman Soi 7. Alongside its curry-noodle bowls, the restaurant serves other northern local specialities and seasonal dishes, keeping the menu rooted in the region rather than only its best-known soup.

A large window looks into the kitchen, so preparing the bowls becomes part of the dining-room experience. The Tourism Authority of Thailand also highlights butterfly-pea tea among its drinks—a quieter detail beside the rich, warming noodle dishes.

sources.label: Tourism Authority of Thailand · Kao Soy Nimman

stops.short: Khao soi is the centre of this Nimman Soi 7 restaurant, with several versions of the northern curry-noodle dish and a kitchen visible through a large window. The next day’s verdict: “I loved kao soy.”

stops.title: Baan Crafts Nimman
paragraphs: The evening browsing is small and tactile: a pastel mug, ceramic animals and the dinosaur plushie you singled out. The lit shopfront closes the sequence and supplies the name.

Baan Crafts Nimman is a craft and gift shop on Nimmanhaemin Road, with smaller handmade objects that can be used or carried every day. Cloth accessories, soft figures and stationery put texture and handwork at a different scale from the furniture workshops south of the city.

Kamlor Handmade’s published stockist lists name Baan Crafts in Nimman Soi 5. The maker’s notebooks use fabric covers, stitching and wood, providing a concrete link between this retail stop and Chiang Mai’s independent makers. The shop belongs to a wider Nimman district known for design-led shops and galleries.

sources.label: Kamlor Handmade · maker’s stockist posts reproduced by Glartent
Tourism Authority of Thailand · Nimmanhemin Road, p12

stops.note: The named storefront and the adjacent evening sequence ground this stop. You also identified the dinosaur plushie photograph with Baan Crafts; it is dated 27 October, not 29 October.
stops.short: Baan Crafts brings small-scale making into Nimman’s shopping streets: fabric accessories, soft toy animals and handmade stationery rather than large furniture. Chiang Mai notebook maker Kamlor lists the Nimman shop among its stockists.

days.title: The forest and the mountain.
days.region: Chiang Mai · Doi Suthep & Tha Phae
days.lede: Forest temples, an amazing drive, a furniture study and dinner in an old mansion.

stops.title: Wat Pha Lat
paragraphs: The morning photographs linger on the moss-covered stupa, white Buddha figures, the temple rooflines and a small forest bridge. Later that day, you called the drive “amazing”; no precise driving route is reconstructed beyond the photographed stops.

Before a road climbed Doi Suthep, monks and worshippers used the forest route through Wat Pha Lat on their way to the mountain’s relic shrine. The temple is therefore part of the pilgrimage landscape, not simply a secluded garden stop.

Chiang Mai University’s Doi Suthep Nature Center identifies the chedi as Burmese in style and places its construction in the era of Kruba Srivichai. The damp setting encourages moss and ferns, especially in the rainy season; beside the temple, the waterfall and a viewpoint connect the buildings to the forest and the city below.

sources.label: Chiang Mai University · Wat Pha Lat nature trail
Tourism Authority of Thailand · Wat Pha Lat

stops.short: Wat Pha Lat belongs to the old pilgrimage route up Doi Suthep. Its Burmese-style chedi stands in humid forest, where moss and ferns soften the masonry and a waterfall runs beside the temple.

stops.title: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep
paragraphs: The photographed naga stairway and nearby temple details place this stop on the mountain after Wat Pha Lat. The broader golden-chedi image is a reference photograph, not a claim about the light or conditions during the visit.

Wat Phra That Doi Suthep is a mountain shrine above Chiang Mai, with a golden chedi containing Buddha relics at its heart. The Tourism Authority of Thailand dates the temple to 1383. Its naga-flanked stairway makes the ascent part of the approach to the sacred precinct.

The mountain road is a much later layer of the story. Followers of the monk Kruba Srivichai built the first paved route in 1935, opening an easier connection between the city and the temple. The elevated setting also explains its role as a landmark visible across Chiang Mai.

sources.label: Tourism Authority of Thailand · Chiang Mai guide, pp14–15

stops.short: A golden relic chedi crowns Chiang Mai’s mountain temple, reached by a ceremonial stairway guarded by naga. The shrine dates to 1383; its modern road is the legacy of Kruba Srivichai’s followers in 1935.

stops.title: A live-edge bench · Teakfurewood Studio?
stops.short: A narrow, live-edge seat, splayed legs and a low stretcher: three angles of the same bench. The likely shop is Teakfurewood Studio, whose Nimman furniture favours the shape and texture of solid timber.
paragraphs: The three photographs turn one bench into a small design study. The overhead view follows the uneven edge of the seat; the lower angle reveals the splayed legs and end stretcher. These are different views of the same photographed object, not catalogue substitutes.

Teakfurewood Studio is the likely location. Its official listing places it on Sirimangkalajarn Soi 13, and a branded public storefront photograph shows a closely related narrow live-edge bench. That supports the identification, but the original images do not show a readable shop sign and their coarse location fix does not establish the store by itself.
stops.note: Probable store identification, not a verified product match. No catalogue model is presented as the exact bench.

sources.label: Teakfurewood · official links and location
Teakfurewood Studio · public storefront reference

stops.title: Kiti Panit · dinner in the old mansion
stops.short: Northern Thai cooking in an 1888 teak mansion on Tha Phae Road. Once a general store, Kiti Panit preserves the founding family’s furniture and restored woodwork, giving dinner the scale and texture of an old house.
paragraphs: The documented dinner is northern pork curry with greens and egg in the old mansion. You remembered it as a delicious meal and clarified that the chocolate shop across the street was not a visit.

Kiti Panit occupies an 1888 teak mansion that began as a general store. The restaurant's history describes its continued connection to the founders' fifth-generation descendants and the restoration of the house by local artists and craftspeople.

Original furniture sits among renewed timber ceilings, floors, panels and stairs. The northern menu includes khao soi, hang le pork curry, sai oua and relishes—regional cooking presented in a building whose commercial history is part of the experience.
stops.note: High-confidence venue match from your old-mansion/across-the-street description, meal images, location and official restaurant context.

sources.label: Kiti Panit · official history and menu
Kiti Panit · official venue

stops.title: Rong Leuy Thapae
paragraphs: The photographs move from the named entrance to a candlelit interior, where towers of red wax stand against old timber and shelves. They record the atmosphere without supplying a particular meal, drink or performance.

Rong Leuy Thapae takes its name from the sawmill that previously occupied the site. The renovated building retains that history through tools and workshop objects used as decoration, rather than replacing it with an anonymous bar interior.

The venue combines northern Thai food, drinks and live music. Behind its compact street entrance is an outdoor seating area, part of the contrast between Tha Phae's close-packed shopfronts and the deeper spaces they conceal.

sources.label: Weekend Magazine · Tha Phae neighbourhood feature
Rong Leuy Thapae · official venue

stops.note: Photographed stop; no meal or drink is assigned to this venue.
stops.short: A former sawmill turned northern Thai restaurant and music venue. Rong Leuy keeps traces of its working past in the décor, while the narrow Tha Phae frontage opens into a larger outdoor space behind.

days.title: A day in wood.
days.lede: A day with wood: village workshops, furniture makers and the carving museum.

stops.title: Baan Tawai
paragraphs: The village visit moves from small furniture and roadside workshops to carving benches. Four films keep the making visible: rough-cut forms, mallet and chisel work, and a longer look at hand-finishing a small wooden chair or stool.

Baan Tawai’s identity rests on woodcarving, furniture and Lanna handicrafts made by local artisans. The Chiang Mai provincial government identifies the Hang Dong village as a craft centre; its workshops and retail spaces put production and display close together.

The range runs from useful household furniture to deeply ornamented sculpture. The nearby Thipmanee collection makes those carving traditions especially legible, with relief panels and freestanding figures rooted in Buddhist and literary subjects. Seen together, the village’s makers show wood as both a construction material and a medium for storytelling.

The photographed Salu Carving Pavilion board honours Baan Tawai’s master woodcarvers. It describes skills passed through generations, a space for live demonstrations and direct purchases from artisans, and encouragement for younger people to learn the craft. The nearby village board names Baan Tawai in Khun Khong, Hang Dong; these are village displays, separate from the museum’s history sign.

sources.label: Chiang Mai Provincial Administrative Organization · Baan Tawai

stops.short: Baan Tawai is a working craft village, not a single showroom. In Hang Dong, south of Chiang Mai, furniture makers and woodcarvers turn timber into everyday tables, intricate reliefs, religious figures and mythical animals.
stops.note: The village entry spans several workshops. Raintree and Dao are separately identified stops within that same visit; the carving clips are not assigned to Thipmanee House.

stops.title: Raintree Furniture
paragraphs: The photographed showroom and RAIN TREE FURNITURE catalogue put broad timber surfaces and table construction in focus. The illustrated designs make this a furniture stop within the wider carving village.

Raintree describes itself as a furniture factory with a shop and showroom, offering both its own designs and work made to customers’ dimensions. Its published business posts include dining tables, cabinets, television units and installation projects—a focus on furnishing rooms rather than producing decorative carvings.

The acacia-and-iron table range gives that approach a clear material language. Wide timber tops show off the grain and natural edge; the metal bases provide a contrasting structure. The result is furniture whose visual interest comes from the wood itself as much as from added ornament.
stops.note: Name directly read from the photographed catalogue; showroom association is supported by the adjoining images and timestamps.

stops.short: Raintree represents the practical furniture-making side of Baan Tawai: broad wood surfaces, iron bases and pieces made to fit a home. Its acacia-table catalogue turns natural grain and irregular edges into the main design features.

stops.title: Dao Handmade
stops.short: Dao Handmade combines teak furniture with ceramics, linen and smaller home objects. Its Baan Tawai range favours useful forms—storage, tables and seating—with woven panels and natural textures bringing detail to otherwise simple woodwork.
paragraphs: The DAO HANDMADE sign appears beside teak furniture; the next photograph moves closer to a tall two-tone ceramic vase. These are the Baan Tawai shop and its display, rather than a different branch in the city.

Dao Handmade’s Baan Tawai business offers wooden furniture, custom design and installation. Its range includes teak shelving, cabinets, consoles, beds and chairs, alongside ceramics, linen and smaller home décor objects.

Woven backs and headboards recur alongside timber frames, giving the furniture a lighter visual texture than solid carved panels. This is another expression of the village’s craft economy: objects designed around daily use, storage and the proportions of a room.
stops.note: Direct sign identification; no Chang Moi branch is substituted.

stops.title: Thipmanee House · Baan Tipmanee
paragraphs: The carved gateway opens onto a sculpture garden, followed by the museum’s own bilingual visitor display and map brochure. These exterior views, the garden film and the display tell the story here; interiors with a posted no-photography notice are not included.

The museum’s visitor display traces Thipmanee House to a small family-run shop established in Baan Tawai in 1994, followed by the museum in 2006. It presents the collection as a way to preserve the knowledge and patience of master woodcarvers; some works, the display says, took up to six years to complete.

Its carvings draw on Lanna, Khmer, Chinese and Hindu traditions. Ganesha gives the museum its name, while Buddhist subjects and animals from literature extend the range. Low relief, high relief and freestanding sculpture show different ways of turning the same material into narrative and ornament.

stops.note: History above is paraphrased from the museum’s own photographed visitor display, with collection context from its official website. Open the gallery to read the display. stops.short: From a family shop founded in 1994 to a museum opened in 2006, Thipmanee preserves Baan Tawai’s carving tradition. Buddhist figures, mythical creatures and Ganesha appear in relief panels and fully sculpted wood.

stops.title: Fleet Motorbike · Fleet CNX
stops.short: Fleet’s scooter shop on Nimman Soi 17 supplied the Yamaha Fazzio for the Chiang Mai days. The rental began on 27 October and ended with the scooter’s return on the 29th, back in the same neighbourhood.
paragraphs: Fleet CNX is a Nimman-based scooter and motorbike rental business. Its range runs from smaller city scooters to larger bikes, with shop pickup and delivery options around Chiang Mai.
The rental record identifies a Yamaha Fazzio 125 cc, activated on 27 October. The scooter was returned on 29 October, closing the two-wheeled part of this trip before the final hotel change.
stops.note: The photographs directly confirm the Fleet storefront on 29 October. They do not establish the exact minute of the scooter return.

sources.label: Fleet CNX · official shop and fleet
Fleet CNX · about

stops.title: Back in Nimman · KaPaO
paragraphs: The photographed KaPaO frontage follows the late lunch of egg-topped food at the table. Its sign and the tightly grouped sequence support placing the meal here; the specific menu variant is not assumed.

KaPaO specialises in Thai holy-basil stir-fries on Nimman Soi 17. The menu offers versions with minced pork, chicken, crispy pork and beef, alongside fried rice. An open kitchen anchors the timber-framed, air-conditioned dining room.

Set meals expand the familiar rice-and-egg format with soup, papaya salad and pickled vegetables. The restaurant's emphasis is on wok cooking and chilli heat rather than a broad, all-purpose Thai menu.
stops.note: Storefront directly confirmed. Meal attribution is inferred from the adjoining sequence, matching dish imagery and approximate location—not GPS alone.

sources.label: Chiang Mai Local · KaPaO
PLANS WITH PAN · KaPaO visit

stops.short: Holy basil, chilli and a hot wok are the focus at KaPaO, a Soi 17 specialist serving stir-fries over rice or as fuller sets. Its open kitchen puts the cooking at the centre of the room.

stops.title: Huen Ui Phat · the last dinner
paragraphs: The previously unnamed dinner is Huen Ui Phat, as you identified it. The two photographs were taken at 20:09 on 29 October: filled rolls with lettuce and a dipping sauce, then sliced pork with two spoon-shaped condiment bowls.

Huen Ui Phat focuses on northern Thai dishes, including hang lay pork curry, khao soi, jackfruit salad and chilli dips. The Nimman dining room combines a traditional wooden-house setting with indoor and outdoor seating; these are venue details, not extra dishes claimed for this meal.

“Scooter returned. Sandals procured.” With the practical loose ends finished, the evening stayed around Nimman. The recorded market journey later places you at Kad Na Mor, leaving there at 21:26 before the final hotel night.

sources.label: Huen Ui Phat · cuisine and location
Huen Ui Phat · dining-room context
Kad Na Mor · map

stops.short: A northern Thai kitchen in Nimman, with regional curries, khao soi and chilli dips. The final dinner’s photographs focus on filled rolls, sliced pork and the little bowls of condiments alongside.
stops.note: Restaurant identification supplied by you. This entry covers the 20:09 dinner photographs; the separately photographed KaPaO meal and frontage at 15:44–16:01 remain their own stop.

stops.title: Stay with Nimman Chiang Mai
stops.short: The final Chiang Mai base stays close to Nimman’s cafés and restaurants. Stay with Nimman combines contemporary interiors with two rooftop pools, on Siri Mangkalajarn Road at the edge of the neighbourhood’s busy lanes.
paragraphs: Stay with Nimman is on Siri Mangkalajarn Road, in the café-and-restaurant district west of Chiang Mai's Old City. Its interiors use contemporary furnishings and warm wood finishes, with several different room layouts across the property.
Two rooftop pools are a distinctive part of the hotel's facilities. The final booking runs from 29 to 30 October, keeping the last night in Nimman after the day's craft shops and scooter return.
stops.note: Confirmed booking dates; arrival-area evidence on 29 October. Booking dates are not exact check-in or check-out times.
